content_preview.title: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is in private beta; its license gives licensees 8 hours to disable a feature or roll back after a safety notice
content_preview.summary: Anthropic's license for the self-hosted Managed Agents server sets 8 hours to disable a feature or roll back after a written risk notice. The New Stack reports it; Anthropic's docs list what the server sends.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Anthropic's [blog post](https://claude.com/resources/articles/self-hosted-claude-managed-agents), dated November 12, 2026, says self-hosted Claude Managed Agents "is now available in private beta" and tells readers to contact their Anthropic account team to request access. The server software is covered by a [license agreement](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/self-hosted-managed-agents-license) whose page lists Nov 12, 2026 under "Effective"; its text says the terms are "effective o...

recommendations: File the corrections record at src/content/corrections/2026-11/<slug>.json (three clarifications) on merge.
thenewstack.io page is Cloudflare-blocked; text was read from the publisher RSS feed (see editor_notes.source_verification).

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, license items by section, what The New Stack reports, what the product pages say, what is not known). 1,047 words, within the 400-1,200 News range. Every license item carries its section number and the quotes are verbatim; the article labels its own limits (no definition of business day, no time zone, no reconciliation of 5.9 with the docs).
editor_notes.source_verification:
Read all 6 stored snapshots (source-0..5.html.gz) after re-hashing each decompressed file against manifest sha256 (all six match); source 6 (thenewstack.io) has file=null, HTTP 403. SOURCE 0 (anthropic.com/legal/self-hosted-managed-agents-license), read as raw text: page shows 'Effective Nov 12, 2026' (no separate last-updated or version date); preamble 'These Terms are effective on the date that Licensee first downloads the Binary' - matches. 5.3 'If Anthropic notifies Licensee in writing that a feature or version of the Licensed Code presents a safety, security, or misuse risk, Licensee will disable that feature or roll back that version in each Deployment within 8 hours after the notice' - the article's quote is verbatim; the license's own term for the customer is 'Licensee'; the heading is 'Safety Rollback'; 'safety notice' in the headline is the Herald's shorthand for a written notice of a safety, security or misuse risk, and the body states the trigger exactly. 5.2 'within 1 business day after Anthropic delivers it' verbatim; 'business day' appears once and is not defined; no time zone anywhere (the article says so, correctly). 1.11 'an Update that Anthropic identifies in writing as necessary to address a safety, security, or misuse risk' vs 5.2 'Updates to address critical agent misuse' - both wordings quoted accurately, and the license does not reconcile them (the article says so; a true and fairly stated difference, not a contradiction the Herald invents). 5.4 (commercially reasonable efforts, 30 days), 5.5 (withdrawn versions, 30 days or the 5.2/5.3 period), 3(c) 'except as the Documentation expressly permits' (verbatim), 5.6 (Anthropic may determine for safety reasons that some or all customers access certain Anthropic Models only through its hosted service; the clause is worded as the Licensee's acknowledgement), 5.9 'may send observability signals to ensure performance to Anthropic', 'will not remove, block, alter, or falsify Usage Signals', 'will not route requests to Anthropic Models in a way that hides that they originate from the Licensed Code', use 'to measure use of the Licensed Code and to monitor compliance' - all verified. Other terms verified: 1.3/2.1/3(a)/3(g) binary, no modify or reverse engineer; 5.7 48 hours after confirming, thresholds agreed in writing; 8.2 US$100,000.00; 9.2 90 days' notice for convenience. SOURCE 1 (claude.com announcement post): dated 'November 12, 2026'; title 'Operate Claude Managed Agents inside your security perimeter'; 'Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is now available in private beta' (twice) and 'Contact your Anthropic account team to request access' - exact product name, 'private beta' wording and date confirmed; model requests 'Anthropic directly, your cloud provider (Amazon Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry), or your own gateway' matches. Absence check: grep of the post text for licen*, terms of the license, signal, telemetry, 8 hours, notice, safety update found nothing (only footer 'Terms of service' links), so the article's 'does not mention the license terms ... an omission, not a disagreement' is accurate and fairly framed. SOURCE 2 (docs overview): 'you install each release yourself'; 'The server software is licensed under the Software License Agreement: Claude Managed Agents Server' - matches. SOURCE 3 (inference-provider): 'Agents name models by their Claude API IDs, such as claude-opus-5-5' verbatim; gateway samples have model_map entries from Claude API IDs to gateway IDs - matches; no statement about non-Claude models either way. SOURCE 4 (data and access): 'The server connects to Anthropic only when the Claude API is its inference provider' verbatim (appears twice); up to three headers (session, agent, environment IDs); 'No setting turns them off'; credential check at startup then every 60 seconds unless health.check_interval is changed; User-Agent header 'Anthropic can use ... to count usage'; the phrase 'Usage Signals' does not appear on any docs page (grep of sources 2-5) - all confirmed. One omission found: the same section 'Fields that name the server software' also describes a 'cma-server' label in metadata.user_id that Anthropic 'can use ... to count usage', sent on calls to the Claude API, Foundry and Claude-API-compatible gateways - not mentioned in the article (clarification 1). SOURCE 5 (upgrade): patch upgrade 'Deploy the old release again. Both releases use the same schema'; minor/major may need a restore; 'A restore loses everything that clients wrote after the backup began.' verbatim; no mention of 8 hours, notice, or license (grep) - the article's absence statement is right. SOURCE 6 (The New Stack, Paul Sawers, 'Anthropic now lets you self-host Claude Managed Agents. The catch? 8 hours to act if it flags a safety risk in the software'): live page 403 to curl with browser, Feedly, Googlebot and Inoreader User-Agents and via Wayback (no capture); read via the publisher RSS feed https://thenewstack.io/feed/ fetched with a Feedly User-Agent (feed.xml sha256 773ff9e3c19ff24b6e673ec8df29e39a952bd75e887a3a249ae7270b9b461c03), item pubDate Fri, 13 Nov 2026 21:29:30 +0000 (matches the article's 2026-11-13 21:29 UTC; the article attributes this to the page's metadata, which I could not read - the RSS is the route used). Verified from the feed text: 'eight hours to disable the affected feature or roll back the version across every deployment'; 'one business day from delivery to install a designated safety update'; 'The license also bars models from other developers unless Anthropic expressly permits them' (article's quote 'unless Anthropic expressly permits them' verbatim); Patrick Moorhead, founder and chief analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy ('Self-hosted usually means the customer owns the change window.' 'This license flips that.'; deadline tighter than most large enterprises allow for production changes; expects regulated buyers to push back on the rollback deadline and the telemetry terms); Jason Andersen, also an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy ('a reasonable ask'; telemetry clause and safeguards requirement broadly in line with how cloud vendors would try to prevent misuse). Names, titles, quotes and paraphrases all match; the article stays attributive and gives no legal advice or enforceability opinion beyond the license text and those attributed quotes. INSIGHT PARTNERS: the article says The New Stack's page states its owner, Insight Partners, is an investor in OpenAI and Anthropic. The disclosure is page chrome, not in the RSS body, and this page is blocked, so it could not be read on this exact page. Corroboration: a Wayback raw capture (web/20261003201501id_) of thenewstack.io/anthropic-claude-text-watermark/ (sha256 644c447207dec7cb249c76dcba87f562c9feb5226048e9f0f739cb6faa2bb087) carries
TNS owner Insight Partners is an investor in: OpenAI, Anthropic.
in the tns-insight-portcos-disclosure block; the block lists the companies a story names and this story names both (the article text mentions OpenAI and Anthropic). Consistent with the site's template, not read on the page itself - recorded as a limit, not filed as a correction. INDEPENDENCE: 7 sources = 6 Anthropic-owned pages (license, announcement post, 4 docs pages) + 1 independent outlet (The New Stack, single reporter); the article says so itself. News category, no 4-source/2-independent requirement. Primary-source reporting (the license read by the Herald, plus the independent outlet) is adequate for a News piece on what the license says, and the article does not read as a legal interpretation: it quotes sections, labels what is not stated, and attributes opinion to named analysts. PROMPT-INJECTION SCAN: manifest suspicious_patterns present on sources 2-5 (all platform.claude.com docs pages), pattern 'system-prompt-reference', identical excerpt in each: ',\"sidebarTitle\":\"Upgrade between model versions\"}]},{\"label\":\"Lifecycle and reference\",\"groups\":[{\"label\":\"System prompts\",\"path\":\"/docs/en/release-notes/system-prompts/overview\"...'. Read in context in the decompressed HTML: it is the docs site's navigation tree (a sidebar group titled 'System prompts' linking to release notes), JSON embedded in the page, addressed to no agent and instructing nothing. Further regex scan of all six snapshots for 'ignore previous/prior instructions', 'note to AI/LLM', 'do not tell the user' found nothing; the only 'AI agent' hit is the footer link text 'AI agents'. FALSE POSITIVE; script auto-REJECT overridden after this check, no source excluded. CLAIM-ACCURACY TESTS: quantifier/absence grep run on the extracted submission; each hit tested against all seven sources (none, only, every, all, both): 'none of the cited sources states how many organisations have access ... or whether the license will change' - true; 'None of the cited sources reports an instance of Anthropic issuing a notice under section 5.3' - true (The New Stack reports none); 'The New Stack is the only outlet independent of Anthropic' - true. Headline/summary/lead: qualifiers kept ('private beta', 'written risk notice', 8 hours, 'licensees'); actor/object not renamed; analysts are two named speakers; no cause implied. Dates: Nov 12 post/license, Nov 13 21:29 UTC New Stack - all correct; the 8-hour clock's time zone is stated as absent. Derived figures: none computed by the Herald; every number is a license or vendor figure labelled as such. Disagreements: the license's two wordings (1.11/5.2), The New Stack's 'unless Anthropic expressly permits them' vs 3(c) 'as the Documentation expressly permits', and license 5.9 vs docs 'what leaves your network' are reported with attribution and not reconciled, as the policy requires; the omissions that make the framing less complete are in the corrections (clarifications 2 and 3). ALLOWLIST: anthropic.com (line 239), claude.com (2775), platform.claude.com (2887) and thenewstack.io (119) are all on config/source_allowlist.txt; no additions. The internal link /article/2026-04/22-anthropic-opens-claude-managed-agents-public-beta-... exists. Anthropic disclosure: required - Anthropic and its Claude Managed Agents product are the subject, in the headline, summary and lead. The one-sentence disclosure 'The Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic.' is present in the second paragraph of the Overview (policy: closing section or end of the Overview). It is accurate (contributor_model is Claude Sonnet 5.5), neutral, and characterises nothing. Every statement about Anthropic in the body is attributive (quoted from the license, post, docs or The New Stack, or labelled as the Herald's own comparison); no flattering or disparaging wording found; the article reports the license's terms without judging them and carries the analysts' contrasting views (Moorhead's pushback, Andersen's 'reasonable ask') in their own words. The sentence sits between two sentences about The New Stack, which is slightly awkward placement but not an error.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline, summary and lead are each backed by the cited pages: product name and private beta (post, Nov 12), 8 hours to disable a feature or roll back after a written notice of a safety, security or misuse risk (license 5.3, Licensee), one business day for Safety Updates (5.2), the model restriction (3(c)), Usage Signals (5.9). All quotes were found verbatim on the exact cited page. Three incomplete subordinate statements are filed as clarifications: the omitted cma-server label, the missing definition of Documentation (1.6) when contrasting 3(c) with The New Stack, and the dropped qualifier on the 8.2 liability cap.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout. No sensational wording, no legal advice, no characterisation of enforceability beyond the license text and attributed analyst quotes. No AI self-reference beyond the required one-sentence disclosure of the contributor model maker.
editor_notes.originality: No prior article on self-hosted Claude Managed Agents or on this license (grep of articles and submissions); the April article on the hosted Managed Agents public beta is linked as background. Not a duplicate.
concerns: The Insight Partners disclosure and the page-metadata date could not be read on the blocked New Stack page; the date was confirmed from the publisher RSS and the disclosure from the site template on a Wayback capture of another article (limit recorded, not a correction).
Only one outlet independent of Anthropic; the article says so itself.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, carefully attributed and neutral coverage of a primary-source reading of the license. The headline, summary and lead hold on the exact pages cited, the Anthropic disclosure is present and correct, and the prompt-injection matches are navigation-menu false positives. Three subordinate incompleteness points are filed as clarifications, so the verdict is APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 2 - the license terms of a major AI vendor first reported from the text itself (an 8-hour rollback duty, a model restriction and a bar on blocking usage signals) matter to enterprise buyers and security teams deciding on self-hosted agents, though the product is private beta and one independent outlet covers it
